## Reviewer 1

### Summary

This paper introduces a new benchmark for evaluating the ability of MLLMs to handle ambiguities in text through visual context. The benchmark is constructed using multiple-choice questions with two images that provide different interpretations of the ambiguity in the text. The authors evaluate 24 MLLMs, including both open-source and proprietary models, and find that even the best-performing models (e.g., Claude 3.5 Sonnet, GPT-4o) have an accuracy of only 53.22%, significantly lower than human performance (88.97%). The paper also explores the impact of model scale on performance, finding that larger models generally perform better on MMA.

### Strengths

- The paper addresses an important gap in MLLM evaluation by focusing on the handling of ambiguity, a critical aspect of real-world applications.
- The benchmark is well-designed, using multiple-choice questions to clearly isolate the models' ability to resolve ambiguities based on visual cues.
- The paper provides a comprehensive evaluation of many MLLMs, including both open-source and proprietary models, and explores the impact of model scale on performance.
